stem: Which condition is triacylglycerol a risk factor for?
rationale: Triacylglycerols are involved in diseases such as obesity, diabetes, and hyperlipoproteinemia.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: What substance is triacylglycerol converted into?
rationale: Triacylglycerols must be hydrolyzed by a lipase to their constituent fatty acids and glycerol before further catabolism can proceed.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > HYDROLYSIS INITIATES CATABOLISM OF TRIACYLGLYCEROLS

stem: What substance is glycerol-3-phosphate converted into?
rationale: Glycerol-3-phosphate is a precursor for the formation of phosphatidylethanolamine.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES

stem: What substance is required for glycerol activation?
rationale: Both glycerol and fatty acid components must be activated by ATP before they can be incorporated into acylglycerols.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES

stem: What substance is phosphatidate converted into?
rationale: Phosphatidate is converted to triacylglycerol in two steps.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES > Biosynthesis of Triacylglycerols

stem: What substrate does monoacylglycerol acyltransferase act on?
rationale: In the intestinal mucosa, monoacylglycerol acyltransferase converts monoacylglycerol to 1,2-diacylglycerol in the monoacylglycerol pathway.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES > Biosynthesis of Triacylglycerols

stem: What substance is phosphatidylcholine converted into?
rationale: An alternative pathway in the liver enables phosphatidylethanolamine to give rise directly to phosphatidylcholine by progressive methylation of the ethanolamine residue. Despite these endogenous sources, choline is considered an essential nutrient for humans and other mammals.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES > Biosynthesis of Phospholipids

stem: What substance is dihydroxyacetone phosphate converted into?
rationale: 1-Alkyldihydroxyacetone phosphate is then converted to 1-alkylglycerol 3-phosphate. After further acylation in the 2 position, the resulting 1-alkyl-2-acylglycerol 3-phosphate is hydrolyzed to give 1-alkyl-2-acylglycerol.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES > Biosynthesis of Glycerol Ether Phospholipids

stem: What substrate does acyltransferase act on?
rationale: Lysophospholipid may be reacylated by acyl-CoA in the presence of an acyltransferase.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES > Phospholipases Allow Degradation & Remodeling of Phosphoglycerols

stem: What substrate do hydrolase enzymes act on?
rationale: The glyceryl phosphoryl base may then be split by a hydrolase, liberating glycerol-3-phosphate plus base.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > TRIACYLGLYCEROLS & PHOSPHOGLYCEROLS ARE FORMED BY ACYLATION OF TRIOSEPHOSPHATES > Phospholipases Allow Degradation & Remodeling of Phosphoglycerols

stem: Which substance is required for the synthesis of ceramide in the endoplasmic reticulum?
rationale: Ceramide is synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum from the amino acid serine (Figure 24-6).
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > ALL SPHINGOLIPIDS ARE FORMED FROM CERAMIDE

stem: What substance is formed when sphingomyelin is converted in the metabolic pathway?
rationale: Sphingomyelins are phospholipids formed when ceramide reacts with phosphatidylcholine, resulting in sphingomyelin plus diacylglycerol (Figure 24-7A).
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > ALL SPHINGOLIPIDS ARE FORMED FROM CERAMIDE

stem: Ceramide is converted into which substance?
rationale: Sphingomyelins are phospholipids formed when ceramide reacts with phosphatidylcholine, resulting in sphingomyelin plus diacylglycerol (Figure 24-7A).
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > ALL SPHINGOLIPIDS ARE FORMED FROM CERAMIDE

stem: GalCer is a major lipid component of which structure?
rationale: GalCer is a major lipid component of myelin.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > ALL SPHINGOLIPIDS ARE FORMED FROM CERAMIDE > Ceramide and One or More Sugar Residues Form Glycosphingolipids

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of glycolipid storage diseases?
rationale: Sphingolipidoses are a group of inherited diseases caused by a genetic defect in the catabolism of lipids containing sphingosine.

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of Tay-Sachs disease?
rationale: In Tay-Sachs disease, the lipid accumulating is GM2 Ganglioside.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > ALL SPHINGOLIPIDS ARE FORMED FROM CERAMIDE > Phospholipids & Sphingolipids Are Involved in Multiple Sclerosis & Lipidoses

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of Fabry disease?
rationale: In Fabry disease, the lipid accumulating is Globotriaosylceramide.

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of Krabbe disease?
rationale: In Krabbe disease, the lipid accumulating is Galactosylceramide.

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of Gaucher disease?
rationale: In Gaucher disease, the lipid accumulating is Glucosylceramide.
citation: chapter_24_metabolism_of_acylglycerols_and_sphingolipids — Metabolism of Acylglycerols & Sphingolipids > ALL SPHINGOLIPIDS ARE FORMED FROM CERAMIDE > Phospholipids & Sphingolipids Are Involved in Multiple Sclerosis & Lipidoses

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of Niemann-Pick disease type A?
rationale: In Niemann-Pick disease types A and B, the lipid accumulating is Sphingomyelin.
